title: Installation and troubleshooting
text: 本文档整理自项目提供的安装说明，并修正了其中会导致安装失败的命令。推荐使用独立的 Conda 环境安装 R、Jupyter 和 PASTRI，避免污染系统环境。

previous_headings: 安装与报错解决
title: Installation and troubleshooting
text: 在 Anaconda Prompt、Miniconda Prompt 或已初始化 Conda 的终端中运行： 原始说明中的 conda create -n R4.2.3_test 没有指定基础软件，且 onda activate 少了首字母 c。不建议继续使用 Python 3.6：该版本已经停止维护，并且容易与当前版本的 Jupyter 依赖冲突。 检查当前环境： 当前环境名称前应显示 *，R 应为 4.2.3，Python 应为 3.10.x。
code: conda create -n PASTRI r-base=4.2.3 python=3.10 -c conda-forge conda activate PASTRI conda info --envs R --version python --version

text: 先安装 Python 内核： 然后启动 R： 在 R 控制台中安装并注册 R 内核： 退出 R 后检查内核：

title: Installation and troubleshooting
text: 原因： Conda 未安装，或当前终端尚未完成 Conda 初始化。 解决： 使用 Anaconda Prompt/Miniconda Prompt； 或在已安装 Conda 的终端执行 conda init； 关闭并重新打开终端后再执行 conda activate PASTRI。

what: EnvironmentNameNotFound: Could not find conda environment
title: Installation and troubleshooting
text: 原因： 环境尚未创建，或环境名输入错误。 解决： 环境名称区分字符，后续命令应始终使用同一个名称 PASTRI。
code: conda info --envs conda create -n PASTRI r-base=4.2.3 python=3.10 -c conda-forge conda activate PASTRI

what: No module named pip 或 No module named ipykernel
title: Installation and troubleshooting
text: 原因： 命令调用了错误环境中的 Python，或当前环境没有安装相应包。 解决： 使用 python -m pip 比直接使用 pip 更容易保证包被安装到当前 Python 环境。
code: conda activate PASTRI conda install pip ipykernel -c conda-forge python -m pip show ipykernel

text: 原因： 通常是 R 依赖包、编译工具或系统库缺失。请向上查找日志中出现的第一条 ERROR，最后一行往往只是汇总信息。 解决顺序： 重新激活 PASTRI 环境； 安装缺失的 R 包； Windows 安装与 R 4.2.x 匹配的 Rtools42； Linux 根据首条错误安装缺失的开发库； 重新执行 remotes::install_github(..., dependencies = TRUE)。 Windows 可检查编译工具：

text: 原因： 网络无法访问 GitHub、仓库地址错误、GitHub API 限流，或缺少 GitHub 凭据。 排查： 若日志显示 API rate limit，可创建 GitHub Personal Access Token，然后在 R 中配置： 不要把 token 写入脚本、README 或提交到 Git。

title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
code: library(PASTRI)  # 1. Load the example lineage tree. tree_file <- system.file("extdata", "HSC.nwk", package = "PASTRI")  # 2. Calculate pairwise LCA features. node_pair_depth <- calculate_lca_depths(   tree.path = tree_file,   mc.cores = 1 )  # 3. Load terminal-cell annotations. cell_file <- system.file("extdata", "HSC_nodeInfos.csv", package = "PASTRI") cell_info <- read.csv(cell_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)  # The order defines the row/column order of every matrix. cell_types <- c("C4", "C5", "C6", "C7", "C8")  # 4. Encode an irreversible progression C4 -> C5 -> C6 -> C7 -> C8. # Rows are destinations and columns are sources. Entries above the diagonal # represent backward transitions and are forbidden here. bound_matrix <- matrix(   Inf,   nrow = length(cell_types),   ncol = length(cell_types),   dimnames = list(cell_types, cell_types) ) bound_matrix[upper.tri(bound_matrix)] <- 0  # 5. Infer the constrained transition matrix. result <- get_optimal_transition_matrix(   node_pair_depth = node_pair_depth,   cell_info = cell_info,   Sel_u = "lca_normalized_height",   fi_depth = 0.2,   Bound_Matrix = bound_matrix,   cell_type_list = cell_types,   mc.cores = 1 )  # Column = start state; row = end state. result$optimal_matrix  # Long-form representation of the same matrix. head(result$optimal_norm_df_dataframe)

what: Calculate Transition Matrix from Two-Cell Correlation — calculate_transition_matrix
title: Calculate Transition Matrix from Two-Cell Correlation — calculate_transition_matrix
text: function calculates cell transition matrices based two-cell correlation functions C(u). first computes frequency cell type (using single-leaf nodes), builds standardized cell type combination avoid duplicate counts. Using node pair depth data selected depth measure (e.g., "lca_normalized_height" "lca_depth"), function computes correlation frequencies depth. depth (maximum threshold fi_depth), corresponding transition matrix computed using eigenvalue decomposition, eigenvalues adjusted according depth. Finally, average transition matrix depths used initial guess optimization procedure (via L-BFGS-B method) derive optimal transition matrix.

title: Get Optimal Transition Matrix — get_optimal_transition_matrix
text: Compute optimal cell transition matrix integrating node-pair depth information per-cell annotations. function: (1) filters terminal (single-leaf) cells selected cell types, (2) calls calculate_transition_matrix() infer best transition matrix structural constraints, (3) flattens matrix long data frame start/end cell-type pairs normalized transition strengths, (4) labels results evaluated depth cutoff. version Windows-safe: internal parallelism automatically coerced single-core Windows vignette building (pkgdown) fail 'mc.cores' > 1 supported Windows.

title: Get Optimal Transition Matrix — get_optimal_transition_matrix
text: node_pair_depth data frame containing node pair depth information (e.g. calculate_lca_depths()). cell_info data frame per-cell info; must contain least cellNum celltype. rows cellNum == 1 retained (terminal leaves), filtered provided cell_type_list. Sel_u Character string choosing depth/height measure use node_pair_depth (e.g. "lca_normalized_height"). fi_depth Numeric. Depth cutoff / threshold passed calculate_transition_matrix(). Bound_Matrix Numeric matrix encoding constraints (e.g. irreversible transitions). Diagonal/upper-triangular structure often encodes prior directionality. cell_type_list Character vector cell types interest, order defines transition structure. mc.cores Integer. Desired parallel cores. Windows silently coerced 1. non-Windows coerced least 1.
